We've now explored the whole picture — the everyday flows and the unusual moments — and your reactions have stopped changing the design. Here's the full scope that's settled:

**Saving**
- Paste a link and press Add; the app fills in the title and the site's summary automatically, in one panel where you review, add tags and your own note, then confirm — keeping saving quick.
- If a page can't be read automatically, you can still save it and fill in the details.
- An empty or invalid entry is politely refused; a bare address without `https://` is accepted.

**Each saved link**
- Shows a site icon, a clickable title that opens the page, the site's summary, your own note (separate, with simple lists/links), tags, and a small de-emphasised address.
- You can correct any of it anytime.

**Finding again (the heart)**
- Search spans address, title, summary and note together, ignoring capitalization, with matches highlighted.
- Power search: `#tag`, `"exact phrases"`, and `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` with parentheses (and those words act as plain text inside quotes); an incomplete query is flagged gently rather than guessed.
- Tags: added with suggestions to reuse spellings; filter by chips, narrowing to items with **all** chosen tags.

**Organising**
- Mark links **To read**; **Archive** to keep them out of the main list; each has its own view with friendly empty states.
- Re-saving a link you already have opens the existing one for editing — never a duplicate — and treats trailing-slash and http/https variants as the same, keeping the secure address.
- Sort by newest, recently updated, oldest, or title; a deliberate **default** in Settings, with the dropdown as a temporary override.

I've also noted for later: cleanly handling very long content and large collections (visual polish/performance), and an explicit "refresh details from the page" action — these are recorded and not part of this build.

**May I now start building this scope for real?** (That's the switch from exploring to implementation — I won't proceed without your go-ahead.)
